setlist.title: Why Don't We Do It In The Road

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dear Mr Fantasy** (4 reviews): Jerry takes over lead vocals from Brent midway, then plays a long, extended guitar lead that stretches the song out; The post-Space Fantasy is called huge, leading into a hot Other One [18][19][22][27]
- **Around And Around** (2 reviews, 1 other source): An Around And Around gets started by mistake after Why Don't We Do It In The Road; Bobby seemingly couldn't get Around And Around going; tapes have been labeled with a joking 'Abort' title [11][19][29]
- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): The first-set Bird Song is singled out as especially tight; Bird Song going into Let It Grow is a stellar pairing in the first set [22][24]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The opener goes wild at the end, with Brent nearly losing his voice [25]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Bobby delivers a mean, hard-edged Little Red Rooster [25]
- **Me And My Uncle** (1 review): Candyman is followed by a well-executed Me And My Uncle into Mexicali Blues [25]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Let It Grow the best version they have heard [24]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The second-set Other One is described as a great version [24]

## Setlist highlights

- **Why Don't We Do It In The Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-06.139531.sbd.pcm.miller-eaton.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1984-07-06.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.86943.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 163 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Some tape-hub bumping noises are audible around the tape flip during Space [2]
- **gd84-07-06.senn441.dodd.13898.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 163 min; rated 3.96/5 by 26 [4]. Said about its sound: The Sennheiser recording sounds tinny with little low end next to the Nak shotgun tapes; Phil is somewhat muted [23]
- **gd1984-07-06.150327.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 22 songs; 162 min [7]. Said about its sound: Levels begin low at Jack Straw, rising about a minute and a quarter into the tune [7]
- **gd1984-07-06.163416.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 164 min [11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls a warm summer evening at Alpine; another show followed the next night [19]
- Reviewer rates the playing as strong as any from 1984 or the decade, with a standout second set [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-06.139531.sbd.pcm.miller-eaton.flac1644**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Recording Info: SBD > PCM Master > Dat; Transfer Info: Dat (Sony PCM-R500) > Tascam DA-3000 > Samplitude Pro X3 Suite > FLAC; All Transfers and Mastering By… [1]. Also: This PCM transfer comes from DATs supplied by Rob Eaton [1]
- **gd1984-07-06.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.86943.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Nakamichi CM-300's w/CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XL-II's, with no Dolby [2]. Also: Nak 300 source with patches from another transfer in Iko Iko, Space and Why Don't We Do It In The Road; Levels adjusted and fades made in Soundforge; TLH used for SBE-OK, FLAC compression and checksums [2]
- **gd84-07-06.senn441.dodd.13898.sbeok.shnf**: source: Fob: Sennheiser 441's > MC > Dat > CdEac >cool edit > shntool > cdwav >shnv3Eac >shn (secure with proper offsets) by Ernie Dodd [4]
- **gd1984-07-06.150327.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew;Sean Murtha;Tom Pinney;Gary Steel;Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: MAUD: Beyer M88's XY 90' > Sony TCD-5M|Maxell MX90 x2 no NR Location: 75 feet from stage DFC- pavilion [7]. Also: First generation from the Pinney master; the start of the recording is missing [7]
- **gd1984-07-06.163416.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5M [11]. Also: Sennheiser 441 source from Alan Matta and Ernie Dodd supplies a patch in Drums and the end of Sugar Magnolia [11]

claims.text: Jerry takes over lead vocals from Brent midway, then plays a long, extended guitar lead that stretches the song out
The post-Space Fantasy is called huge, leading into a hot Other One
An Around And Around gets started by mistake after Why Don't We Do It In The Road
Reviewer recalls a warm summer evening at Alpine; another show followed the next night
The first-set Bird Song is singled out as especially tight
The end of Space flowing into Dear Mr. Fantasy is praised as especially nice
The Sennheiser recording sounds tinny with little low end next to the Nak shotgun tapes; Phil is somewhat muted
Reviewer rates the playing as strong as any from 1984 or the decade, with a standout second set
Reviewer calls this Let It Grow the best version they have heard
Bird Song going into Let It Grow is a stellar pairing in the first set
The second-set Other One is described as a great version
The opener goes wild at the end, with Brent nearly losing his voice
Bobby delivers a mean, hard-edged Little Red Rooster
Candyman is followed by a well-executed Me And My Uncle into Mexicali Blues
Dear Mr. Fantasy launches a run through The Other One, Black Peter and Why Don't We Do It In The Road
Bobby seemingly couldn't get Around And Around going; tapes have been labeled with a joking 'Abort' title
Sugar Magnolia follows and rescues the band after the failed Around And Around
This PCM transfer comes from DATs supplied by Rob Eaton
Nak 300 source with patches from another transfer in Iko Iko, Space and Why Don't We Do It In The Road
Some tape-hub bumping noises are audible around the tape flip during Space
Levels adjusted and fades made in Soundforge; TLH used for SBE-OK, FLAC compression and checksums
First generation from the Pinney master; the start of the recording is missing
Levels begin low at Jack Straw, rising about a minute and a quarter into the tune
Master cassette source from Stephen Thomas, transferred by Charlie Miller, who coordinated the release
Sennheiser 441 source from Alan Matta and Ernie Dodd supplies a patch in Drums and the end of Sugar Magnolia
A brief Around & Around tease comes just before Sugar Magnolia
